standard_prerequisites.name: Symmetric interval exchange transformation
standard_prerequisites.statement: An IET is symmetric when the reflection of the whole interval conjugates it to its inverse off the discontinuities.

standard_prerequisites.name: Symmetric subinterval
standard_prerequisites.statement: A subinterval is alpha-symmetric when it is centred at the middle point c_alpha of the exchanged interval I_alpha.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the class of intervals on which the computation is performed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reflection of the centres
standard_prerequisites.statement: The conjugate of the transformation by the reflection of the whole interval fixes the middle point of each continuity interval.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the identity that converts the shifted centre back into the centre.

core_obligations: Write the symmetric subinterval as the interval centred at c_alpha with some radius, inside the exchanged interval, and fix a point of it expressed as the centre plus an offset (source line 605).
Use that the transformation restricted to the exchanged interval is a translation, so that it sends the centre plus offset to the image of the centre plus the offset (source lines 607-609).
Apply the identity that the conjugate fixes the centre and the reflection reverses the offset, obtaining a point of the subinterval again, which is exactly the statement (source lines 609-612).

proof_roadmap.step: Parametrise the symmetric subinterval and its points by an offset from the centre.
Use the translation property and the identity for the centre to compute the image.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 596-602: for a symmetric interval exchange transformation and an alpha-symmetric subinterval, the conjugate of the transformation by the reflection of the whole interval maps the interior of the subinterval onto itself and agrees there with the reflection of the subinterval. The proof (source lines 604-613) is a computation that only becomes possible after two rewritings: the points of the subinterval are expressed as the middle point of the exchanged interval plus an offset, which uses that the subinterval is centred there, and the transformation restricted to the exchanged interval is a translation, so the conjugate of the centre plus offset becomes the conjugate of the centre plus the offset; the identity that the conjugate fixes the centre then turns the result into the reflected point. The statement records neither the parametrisation nor the translation step.
